page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 7.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of approximately 0.9 GB per core. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled to deliver 2 threads per core. It includes a 45 MB L3 cache and supports hardware-level instructions such as AVX, AES cryptography, and FMA. This instance does not bundle local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate that the n1-highcpu-8 delivers modest performance characteristics. Its single-core and multi-core CPU capabilities are positioned in the lower tiers, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1109.79 and a multi-core score of 5820.12. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, reaching 47.28 GB/sec for read operations and 34.7 GB/sec for write operations, though small-block cached reads are relatively weak at 325.55 GB/sec. Computational tasks like ray tracing achieve average marks, while text processing and compression workloads show poor performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-highcpu-8 represents an older hardware generation within the Google Cloud portfolio. It offers a budget-friendly entry point for compute-heavy tasks that require multiple dedicated vCPUs but have minimal memory requirements. This profile is suitable for workloads such as basic batch processing, lightweight build and compilation pipelines, and simple web serving where high memory capacity is not a prerequisite.
